about.heroDescription: KARURA unites students from {count} institutions across Japan and the U.S. to build, test, and compete with a Mars rover, and to show that international engineering collaboration at the student level is both possible and world-class.
about.missionLead: The University Rover Challenge is the world's most demanding robotics competition for university students, held every year on Mars-analog terrain in Utah.
about.missionBody: KARURA was built on a simple thesis: the most advanced rover on the field should also be the most internationally diverse team on the field. We compete at URC every year, and in 2024 we proved that thesis true by reaching the Finals as the first Japanese and first international team in competition history.
about.missionBody2: Our mission is not limited to competition podiums. Every system we engineer, every student who joins from a new university, and every sponsorship we build moves the needle on international space collaboration as a practical, replicable model.
about.missionBody3: KARURA connects Japanese engineering excellence with the American aerospace research ecosystem at Texas A&M, combining complementary perspectives to solve hard engineering problems.
about.differentiatorsItem1Body: We are not an exchange program. We are a permanent dual-node organization with engineering operations running in Japan and Texas at the same time.
about.differentiatorsItem2Body: Every subsystem has been field-tested at URC on Mars-analog desert terrain. Our 2024 build reached the Finals, and the hardware performs under pressure.
about.differentiatorsItem3Body: 30+ institutions across Japan and the U.S., giving KARURA unrivaled access to diverse engineering talent and research resources.
about.networkDescription: Students from these institutions form the engineering backbone of KARURA across all five departments.

whySponsor.description: Sponsorships with KARURA are not logo placements, they are engineering deployments. Your components, your technology, and your brand travel to one of the world's most demanding robotics competitions.

realWorld.title: Real-world field testing
realWorld.body: Your technology operates in Mars-like terrain, extreme UV, loose sediment, and temperature swings. It is the most credible field validation available to a student-engineering sponsor.

pipeline.title: Cross-Pacific talent pipeline
pipeline.body: 100+ engineers from 30+ universities across Japan and Texas A&M. Sponsors gain direct access to a bilingual, internationally collaborative engineering cohort before they enter industry.

brand.title: Institutional brand placement
brand.body: KARURA competes in front of NASA judges, aerospace industry observers, and a global press audience. Your logo is on the hardware being filmed and photographed throughout.

hero.description: Three generations of competition-proven Mars rover hardware. Engineered across two countries, tested in Utah, refined for the next launch window.

competition.description: The University Rover Challenge scores teams across four mission categories. Each task is evaluated against Mars-analog conditions in the Utah desert, with scoring weighted by task completion percentage and time.

navigation.name: Autonomous Navigation
navigation.description: Rover must navigate 1+ km of rocky Mars-analog terrain, identifying and reaching GPS waypoints without any human intervention.
navigation.challenge: No-comms zone for portions of the run. Terrain includes loose rock, slopes, and dry river beds.

servicing.name: Equipment Servicing
servicing.description: The rover must operate a cache of hand tools, including levers, buttons, and valves, using only the robotic arm and end-effector.
servicing.challenge: Requires sub-centimeter arm precision. All tools resemble real-world industrial hardware.

retrieval.name: Extreme Retrieval
retrieval.description: Navigate extreme terrain gradients and narrow passages to retrieve a cache object from a designated location and return it to base.
retrieval.challenge: Maximum slope angles exceed 40°. Terrain designed to challenge all 6 wheels simultaneously.

science.name: Science Mission
science.description: Identify, document, and collect soil and rock samples from a designated site. Perform onboard analysis to detect potential biosignatures.
science.challenge: Samples must be documented in-situ with GPS coordinates, images, and onboard spectral analysis.

hero.description: Build competition-proven Mars rover systems alongside students across Japan and Texas. Explore open roles, understand our international workflow, and become part of the next URC campaign.

portal.heading: Build the next generation of Martian systems.
